chunks: Call to the path of your Lord with wisdom and good advice, and argue with them in the best way. Indeed, your Lord is the Knower of those who stray from His path, and He is the Knower of those who are guided.

key_terms.الْحِكْمَةِ: Wisdom; deep understanding and appropriate application of knowledge in calling to God.
key_terms.بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ: With that which is best; using the most appropriate and gentle manner in debate.
key_terms.بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ: The guided ones; those who follow the right path.
key_terms.وَالْمَوْعِظَةِ الْحَسَنَةِ: Good advice or exhortation; eloquent and gentle preaching.
key_terms.وَجَادِلْهُمْ: And argue/debate them; engaging in discourse with others.

ai.seo_question: What are the three methods of da'wah (invitation to God) mentioned in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often viewed as the foundational principle of da'wah, where 'wisdom' (hikmah) refers to adapting the message to the listener's capacity, and 'good preaching' (maw'izah hasanah) denotes sincere, heart-touching advice. The concluding clause, 'He knows best who strays and who is guided,' serves as a theological reassurance for the caller, emphasizing that the responsibility lies with the messenger to convey the truth effectively, while ultimate guidance is a divine prerogative, a concept deeply linked to the doctrine of divine justice and human free will.
